rawCandidates.selectionReason: Skincare benefit section shows calm product/service explanation and CTA discipline, with claim language to heavily restrict.
Short assessment/enquiry form, consent microcopy, and single-path CTA map to first consultation intake.
Consult-first process hierarchy is directly useful for positioning skin planning before treatments.
Full-bleed skincare product staging is useful as a visual reference and an outcome-claim anti-reference.
Treatment/category rail and trust bullets are useful only if stripped of medical/provider claims.
Product card/service card structure with learn-more and safety-information links maps to treatment menu governance.
Beauty/wellness search-led homepage maps to service, location, date, and consultation decision controls.
Local wellness venue detail shows contact/map/service proof layout, but ratings and photos are unsafe unless supplied.
Consultation row, hours, and map are useful for local service truth and booking/enquiry structure.
Dark introduction CTA band can become a consultation handoff without copying customer logos.
Professional service-detail page is a useful model for phase breakdown and request-to-book flow.
Large independent-professional typography gives a premium owner-led alternative to clinic templates.
Regulated-adjacent process bullets and help-line framing are useful for careful skin-consult claims.
How-visits-work structure helps describe consultation steps without promising treatment results.
Icon-based what-to-expect sequence maps well to enquiry, consult, plan, and aftercare.
FAQ/search page is useful for regulated-adjacent answer navigation and consultation prep.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make consultation the first safe decision before facials, peels, or treatment planning.
Explain what happens before, during, and after the consult instead of selling treatment outcomes.
Use process proof and intake clarity while withholding medical/provider proof unless supplied.
Use privacy-safe consult artifacts, ingredient-neutral objects, or owner-approved room photos instead of result photos.
Any claim about results, provider credentials, prescriptions, ingredients, or safety must be source-backed or removed.

bannedUses: Do not copy Hims telehealth claims, licensed-provider wording, product outcomes, shipping language, or medical authority.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Hero can lead with treatment concern, consult type, and preferred contact path rather than a gallery.
One dominant enquiry CTA should stay visible near concern/service selection.
Search controls should collapse into stacked mobile rows with clear labels for consult, facial, peel, or plan.
The enquiry path should capture concern, prior treatments, sensitivity, and contact preference without asking for clinical data publicly.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fresha's marketplace brand, appointment-count proof, account menu, app CTA, gradient, or exact search component.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Treatment cards should include concern, consult-first caveat, who it may suit, and enquiry action.
Cards need selected, unavailable, learn-more, and enquiry-started states.
Use soft neutral surfaces for service cards, with restrained borders instead of heavy shadows.
Treatment cards and safety links need explicit button labels, focus states, and large touch targets.

bannedUses: Do not copy product names, prices, prescription tags, safety-information legal language, face closeups, or buy-now e-commerce behavior.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use confident editorial scale to make the consult room feel specialist without copying clinic authority language.
Write as a calm practitioner: plain concern, careful next step, no miracle-skin adjectives.
Pair a strong owner-led headline with concise service labels and a consult artifact.
Let type scale, whitespace, and section rhythm create depth before shadows or glass effects.

bannedUses: Do not copy Contra's portfolio labels, waitlist state, designer identity, location copy, or gradient footer strip.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: The consult request can be a short staged intake: concern, skin sensitivity, prior treatment, preferred contact.
Use Wellington location/contact labels and avoid US state, telehealth, or prescription framing.
Tokenize input height, border, surface, microcopy, and CTA size so intake states remain stable.
A static intake module and service cards should replace heavy photo/video sections until assets are approved.

bannedUses: Do not copy price, state selector, free visit, prescription consent, telehealth legal copy, or product subscription flow.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Give cautious claims room to breathe; dense beauty copy will read like overpromising.
Use a calm meadow/cream palette with one action accent, not clinical blue or beauty pink overload.
Use abstract skin maps, consultation cards, or product-neutral objects instead of borrowed result photos.
Visible consult, facial, peel, aftercare, and enquiry facts should map to truthful agent-readable page metadata.

bannedUses: Do not copy insurance language, watch imagery, policy claims, help-line promise, or serif composition wholesale.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use simple utility icons for consult, skin plan, treatment choice, and aftercare only where they clarify the step.
If motion is used, limit it to step reveal or selected concern transition; no cosmetic transformation animation.
Soft rounded panels can signal care, but avoid making every section a floating card.
The process sequence should be the proof until real reviews, photos, credentials, or policies are supplied.

bannedUses: Do not copy medication steps, provider prescription claims, pharmacy pickup, condition-count badges, or medical icons exactly.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Consultation rows should route to enquiry, not invented live booking or price promises.
Location, hours, currency, and phone/email formats must match owner-supplied Wellington facts.
Map, hours, service rows, and contact actions need text equivalents and keyboard paths.
Local details should stack below the consult CTA on mobile without hiding the primary enquiry action.

bannedUses: Do not copy Square demo business, fake map, Menlo Park address, sample prices, block-extra-time copy, or book-now availability.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Full-bleed product imagery plus proven-skincare/outcome claims would overpromise for a local consult-room fixture.
Result-oriented anti-aging copy and product photography risks unverified treatment claims.
Generic AI service-card layout would weaken clinical trust and look template-made.
Dark portfolio/editor UI is not a client-facing skin consult reference and would leak tool-surface noise.

remixDirection.summary: A consult-first skin room page with calm owner-led editorial type, privacy-safe treatment artifacts, careful concern/service routing, a short enquiry intake, and process proof that avoids result claims until the owner supplies evidence.
selectedMoves: Hims-inspired consult-first process hierarchy, stripped of telehealth, prescription, provider, and outcome claims.
Fresha-inspired service/concern selector, rebuilt as an enquiry path for consults, facials, peels, and treatment planning.
Contra-inspired owner-led editorial type to avoid generic clinic templates.
HODINKEE-inspired regulated-adjacent restraint for careful claim handling and FAQ-style reassurance.
Square-inspired local service detail structure for hours, contact, and consultation rows without fake booking availability.
Hims what-to-expect sequence adapted into consult, plan, treatment choice, and aftercare steps.
explicitRejects: No invented results, before-and-after photos, reviews, credentials, ingredients, treatment prices, safety claims, medical/provider claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
No copied product photography, telehealth language, marketplace appointment counts, fake map data, or SaaS-style trust badges.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted screen.
